title: Characterization of spectral degree
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $B$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ whose constant-one element is indexed by $0$ and which is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product. For a positive integer $n$, a function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and $k\in\mathbb N$, the spectral degree of $f$ is at most $k$ if and only if every Fourier coefficient indexed by a multi-index whose number of nonzero coordinates exceeds $k$ is zero.
hypotheses_covered: Finite nonempty basis index set $\iota$ with decidable equality
A basis element indexed by $0$ is constant one
The basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
